mechanism_narrative: A continued increase in WORKPLACES mobility raises weekday trip chaining and lunch-time shopping, which lifts RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks relative to the last four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES improved from -7.9 to -2.9 before easing to -6.7
failure_condition: If WORKPLACES does not rise for at least two of the next four weeks and RETAIL_REC still increases, this mechanism is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: When RESIDENTIAL stays elevated while TRANSIT remains muted, households substitute toward nearby discretionary shopping and restaurant trips, pushing RETAIL_REC up within two weeks.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT stays below 5 points while RESIDENTIAL stays above 4 points
failure_condition: If TRANSIT remains below 5 and RESIDENTIAL remains above 4 for the next two weeks but RETAIL_REC fails to improve, the hypothesis fails.

mechanism_narrative: A renewed decline in TRANSIT signals tighter travel frictions or fewer downtown visits, which suppresses RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks because fewer cross-neighborhood shoppers reach retail centers.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT falls by 3 or more points week-on-week
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT peaked at 5.1 in t-1w then fell to 3.0 in t-0w
failure_condition: If TRANSIT drops by at least 3 points week-on-week and RETAIL_REC still rises over the next month, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in PARKS activity diverts discretionary time away from shopping, so retail-and-recreation mobility falls over the next one week when parks demand is the dominant leisure outlet.
candidate_trigger: PARKS rises above -15 points after being below -20 points
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS moved from -21.4 to -19.6 to -18.7 across the last three weekly means
failure_condition: If PARKS rises above -15 after having been below -20 and RETAIL_REC does not weaken in the next week, this mechanism fails.

mechanism_narrative: Improvement in both GROCERY_PHARM and WORKPLACES increases routine out-of-home mobility, and that routine spillover raises RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks more than either series alone.
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM rose to 8.3 in t-1w while WORKPLACES improved to -2.9
failure_condition: If both GROCERY_PHARM and WORKPLACES rise for two consecutive weeks but RETAIL_REC remains below its prior four-week mean, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: If RESIDENTIAL falls while WORKPLACES also fall, consumers are staying home rather than commuting, and RETAIL_REC will decline within two weeks as both discretionary and incidental trips weaken.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL declines below 5 and WORKPLACES declines below -5
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL was 5.4 at t-0w and WORKPLACES was -6.7 at t-0w
failure_condition: If RESIDENTIAL stays above 5 and WORKPLACES stays below -5 but RETAIL_REC rises over the next two weeks, the hypothesis fails.

mechanism_narrative: A broad retreat in GROCERY_PHARM and TRANSIT indicates reduced essential-trip activity and lower public circulation, which depresses RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT falls below 2 and GROCERY_PHARM falls below 3
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT fell from 5.1 to 3.0 and GROCERY_PHARM fell from 8.3 to 4.7 in the latest week
failure_condition: If TRANSIT drops below 2 and GROCERY_PHARM drops below 3 but RETAIL_REC does not weaken over the next month, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: In hot-weather leisure periods, elevated PARKS mobility and elevated RESIDENTIAL time jointly pull activity toward home and open-air recreation, so RETAIL_REC softens over the next one to four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS remained deeply negative while RESIDENTIAL stayed positive across all four weeks
failure_condition: If PARKS stays elevated relative to its recent baseline and RESIDENTIAL remains above 4 but RETAIL_REC rises over the next four weeks, the hypothesis fails.
